item.title: Cold Chain and Yard Safety
item.description:
Runink FACE · Reactive logistics

This is a Runink FACE scenario, its yard-facing end. It is an illustration of the mechanism, not an account of a deployment. What the software reads here is the paperwork and the images a cold chain already produces — the consignment record, the handover, the photograph taken at the door — against the rule that governs the shipment. What FACE is.

item.title: Customer Data Privacy and Audit Records
item.description:
Runink FACE · Compliance and audit records

This is a scenario for Runink FACE. The checks described here read FACE's own records of your shipments and reports, and they are part of FACE itself.

In Short

  • Personal details do not reach the logs. Email addresses, phone numbers, card numbers, national insurance numbers and IP addresses are stripped out of log and diagnostic output before it is written, so the trail a system leaves behind does not become a second copy of the data.
  • It is built into the platform, not a report you run. The stripping happens on the logging path underneath every service, at every place a service writes a line.
  • Every check keeps its own working. What was read, the rule it was read against, what was found and who looked at it are kept on the record, and a check that could not run is written down as exactly that.

A Trail Nobody Has Time To Check.

Personal details travel with every record, and every system that handles a record leaves a trail behind it. Answering for that trail means joining systems by hand.

item.title: Freight Claims and Port Charges
item.description:
Runink FACE · Freight claims

This is a scenario for Runink FACE — the Fulfilment Autonomous Claims Engine. Claims are not a side feature here. They are the C in the product's name.

In Short

  • The paperwork is gathered for you, and only the parts that are really there. The entry, the port, the reason it is held, the documents that are missing, the days it has been held and the per-day charge arrive in one place, joined to the shipment they belong to.
  • Quantities are checked three ways. The purchase order, the invoice and the bill of lading are compared against each other, and where they disagree the finding names the pair and the size of the gap — bill of lading against order, bill of lading against invoice.
  • The letter is drafted, not sent. A named person reads the case, edits or rejects it, and that sign-off is kept on the record. Nothing goes to the carrier before it.

Claims That Expire Quietly.

Most claims are not lost arguments. They are claims nobody had the morning to assemble, filed too late or never filed at all.

item.title: Re-Running the Route After the Day Has Changed
item.description:
In Short

  • A route comes back as a distance, a duration and a line on the map. An origin, a destination and the constraints you named go out to the routing provider; what comes back is a measured road distance and a travel time, not an opinion.
  • No money is attached to it, on purpose. The routing provider returns distance and time and no cost. So no saving is printed next to the route, because a figure nobody measured sitting beside two that were is how an estimate gets quoted as a fact.
  • When it could not be worked out, it says so. No routing credential on the connection, or a provider that returns nothing, comes back as unavailable. It comes back saying so, rather than with the fields left empty, which on a screen is indistinguishable from a good answer.

Optimal At Six. Not At Ten.

The plan was good when it was built. Then a drop took forty minutes longer than it should have, a road shut, and a customer moved a window. The plan is now the best answer to a question nobody is asking.

item.title: Returns and What to Do With Them
item.description:
Runink FACE · Reverse logistics

This is a Runink FACE scenario, its returns and circular-economy side. What follows is what the product is built to do and how it would run against your own records. It is an illustration of the mechanism, not an account of a deployment. What FACE is.

In Short

  • The call is drafted at the scan. FACE works from four things the dock hands it: the return's id, the barcode, the condition grade the person at the dock wrote down, and the item's value as they type it. It answers at the moment the box lands rather than the afternoon somebody gets to the pen.
  • The policy is written down, so the same grade always gets the same answer. Restock, refurbish, recycle, dispose — each condition grade routes to one of them, the same way every time, whoever is on the dock and whatever the queue looks like. A grade it does not recognise is refused rather than filed under its best guess.
  • The recovery figure is arithmetic you can check. The triage returns an estimated recovery yield and a refurbishment cost, and both are the value the dock entered multiplied by a fraction fixed against the grade: pristine yields 95% of that value and nothing to refurbish, damaged yields 75% and a quarter of it as the repair.
  • The person at the dock makes the call. The triage answers the screen, and the decision stays with the person holding the box.

A Return Is Worth Most On Day One.

Most of what a return loses, it loses while it waits. Not in the repair, not in the freight — in the weeks it sits in a corner of the dock while somebody works out where it should go.

item.title: Stock Cover and Supplier Planning
item.description:
Runink FACE · Inventory fulfillment

This is a Runink FACE scenario, the fulfilment side of it. What follows is what the product is built to do and how it would run against your own records. It is an illustration of the mechanism, not an account of a deployment. What FACE is.

In Short

  • The trigger says which bound it crossed, in words. The reorder point, the minimum and the maximum are the ones you already run. What it returns is the bound that was crossed and the level that crossed it, written out, so the warning can be argued with instead of acknowledged.
  • The forecast says how much to trust it. Every projection names the model, which was picked by holding back the most recent stretch of your own history and refitting each candidate on what came before it, and how many periods it had to learn from. When a line's history does not predict itself, that is one of the findings too.

Stop Finding Out Too Late.

A stockout warning that arrives after the safety stock is gone is not a warning. It is a bill for air freight with a few days' notice.

item.title: Talking to Drivers Without a Screen
item.description:
Runink FACE · Reactive logistics, driver-facing

This is a Runink FACE scenario, the driver-facing end of it. What follows is what the product is built to do and how it would run against your own fleet records. It is an illustration of the mechanism, not an account of a deployment. What FACE is.

In Short

  • The driver asks out loud and hears the answer. Where the next stop is, what the customer asked for, which door to use. No screen to read and no reason to pull over. Every conversational reply is synthesised inside the FACE process itself, from a voice embedded in the binary, and the speech coming in goes to the model server you already run — the one inference endpoint you point FACE at, carrying an audio-capable model — rather than to a speech API somebody else operates.
  • It is a phone call, so it goes over the phone network. The leg between the cab and the building is carried by a telephony provider, the same as any other call your drivers make. What that provider never gets is the text: the transcription, and the reasoning that produces the answer, happen on your machines, and the spoken reply is encoded there too. The provider carries the audio, as it does for any call.
  • What the call produces is a transcript, on the record. Both sides of the conversation are written to the call log, speaker by speaker, so the hour at the gate is recorded the moment it is said. An urgent word on the call does raise something. The same six words are watched on the phone as on the text side — urgent, asap, emergency, broken, failing, late — and a match both changes how the agent answers and sends the caller's own sentence to the manager number you configured. Somebody named on the desk reads the log and makes the change.

Hands On The Wheel.

A driver who has to read a screen to answer a question will either stop the truck or read it while moving. One costs you the hour. The other costs you much more, one day.

item.title: Testing a Plan Before You Commit to It
item.description:
Runink FACE · Financial scenarios and hypothesis testing

This is a scenario for Runink FACE, the Fulfilment Autonomous Claims Engine. FACE runs on the Runink TIDE platform, but the work on this page is FACE's own.

In Short

  • The change has to be written down before it can be argued. A hypothesis is stated explicitly, together with the rules it touches — the reorder points, the lead times, the service commitments your business already runs on. Most of the value is in that step, and it is the step normally skipped.
  • What comes back is reasoning, ranked, with the rule it invoked. Each consequence is tied to the specific rule it follows from, so you can disagree with it on the merits. It is an argument you can check, not a number to accept.
  • Your live systems stay untouched. The engine reasons over the rules you gave it, where FACE runs, and the scenario goes to no outside AI service.
  • You can make it rough on purpose. Push a lane a week late. Drop a supplier. Let a load run warm. Plans that only work when everything goes right show it here, not at the quarter end.

Write The Plan Down Before You Argue It.

When a port shuts or a plant stops, you have about a day to pick a new route. The numbers that would settle it sit in four systems, and pulling them together takes longer than the choice can wait.

item.title: The Picture Nobody Has Time to Assemble
item.description:
In Short

  • Your records are sorted by what they are, not by where they came from. Two tables about shipments both belong to logistics whether one arrived from your warehouse system and the other as a spreadsheet somebody emails on Fridays.
  • The map is derived, not guessed. The domains and the joins between them are worked out by fixed rules from the records your connected sources return: their column names and a small sample of rows. No model and no web search take part in that step, and the same records always produce the same map.
  • A domain it could not assess is marked as not assessed. Not as a pass. The words are explicit: this is not a finding that the area is fine.

Four Systems. One Morning You Do Not Have.

Nothing is missing. Every fact you need was recorded, correctly, by somebody doing their job. It is the joining that never happens in time.

item.title: When Demand Turns Before the Plan Does
item.description:
In Short

  • The season and the trend are pulled apart. Your own history is decomposed into the underlying trend, the repeating seasonal shape and what is left over. The leftovers are where a turn shows up first.
  • The forecast says which method produced it, and why that one. Competing models are tried against periods your history already contains, and the one that predicted those periods best is the one that is used. The answer carries the name of the method that won.
  • A series it cannot fit is refused, not fitted anyway. Too few periods, or no model that holds, comes back saying so. It does not come back as a confident-looking line with nothing under it.

The Signal Turned Before The Plan Did.

A line starts moving long before the reorder point moves. The gap between those two dates is the whole problem, and it is usually settled by the time anyone is told.

item.title: Which Clause Governs This, and Who Checked
item.description:
Runink FACE · Paralegal and compliance review

This is a scenario for Runink FACE, the Fulfilment Autonomous Claims Engine. The agent doing this work is written to a stated role — paralegal and compliance officer — and that role defines exactly what it does. It reads, it cites, and it hands the reading to somebody who decides.

In Short

  • It finds the clause and the record, and shows you both. Nothing comes back asserted. Every finding arrives with the passage it was read from and the record it was held against.
  • It writes notes, not changes. It is built to hand back a next step in business language — draft this letter, raise this ticket, escalate this to the data protection officer. It is explicitly forbidden from writing a fix into your systems.
  • “Checked and clean” and “could not check” are different entries. Most tools collapse both into a green tick. Here the second one is a state in its own right, with three separate ways of arriving at it — nothing came back, what came back could not be parsed, what came back was empty — and the wording it produces says outright that this is not a finding that the area is compliant. It is the entry an audit is actually hunting for.

A Lookup That Should Take Ten Minutes.

Somebody asks whether the agreement permits this. A paragraph somewhere settles it. Finding the paragraph takes a day and a half, so the question gets answered from memory.

item.title: Your Adjusters Spend the Day Gathering, Not Deciding
item.description:
Runink FACE · Insurance, inside the Finance domain

This is a scenario for Runink FACE, the Fulfilment Autonomous Claims Engine. Insurance is not a separate product or a separate module: FACE types claims, reserves, premiums, deductibles, settlements and underwriting records into its Finance domain, on the reasoning that a claim is a reserve held against a policy.

In Short

  • The file is assembled. It is not judged. The wording, the loss documents, the reserve movements and the authority limit that applies at that value arrive in one place, joined to the claim they belong to.
  • Every reading says where it came from. Text lifted out of a document comes back with the file it was read from and the method used to read it, so a figure in the draft can be traced to a page rather than taken on trust.
  • The decision is not the software's to make. It drafts the next step. An underwriter or a claims lead approves it, rewrites it or throws it out, and their name stays on the record beside what they decided.

The Gathering Is The Job. The Judgement Should Be.

An adjuster's morning goes on finding the wording, the loss report and last quarter's reserve movement. The part that actually needed their training takes ten minutes at the end of it.
